paper_title: Supersymmetric AdS solitons and the interconnection of different vacua of N = 4 Super Yang-Mills (Anabalon, 2024, JHEP)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\textbf{Claim.}
Let \(s\in\{-1,+1\}\) and suppose a non-degenerate charge-equality branch satisfies
\[
q_2=sq_1,\qquad q_1\delta\psi_1\psi_2\neq0,\qquad x_0>0,\qquad x_0\neq1.
\]
Then the Wilson-line sources and the source cubic force
\[
x_0=-s\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1},\qquad 2\psi_1-s\psi_2=\pm1.
\]
Moreover the normalized holographic energy vanishes on this branch:
\[
F_\Phi=0.
\]
Thus the five-dimensional supersymmetric branch \(q_2=-q_1\) and the additional ten-dimensional sign \(q_2=q_1\) project to the two source-only loci
\[
q_2=-q_1:\quad x_0=\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1},\quad 2\psi_1+\psi_2=\pm1,
\]
\[
q_2=q_1:\quad x_0=-\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1},\quad 2\psi_1-\psi_2=\pm1.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &q_1(1-x_0^{-1})\delta=2\pi\psi_1,
\qquad q_2(1-x_0)\delta=2\pi\psi_2.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &q_2=sq_1,
\qquad s\in\{-1,+1\}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &x_0>0,
\qquad x_0\neq1,
\qquad q_1\delta\psi_1\psi_2\neq0.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &P(x_0)=0,\text{ where}\\
&P(x):=\psi_1^2x^3+
\bigl(\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2\bigr)x^2\\
&\hspace{36mm}-\psi_2^2\bigl(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1\bigr)x+
\psi_2^4.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &F_\Phi=-16\frac{(\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2)(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2)}{x_0(x_0-1)^2}.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{The ten-dimensional supersymmetry condition allows }|q_1|=|q_2|.
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Divide the two Wilson-line equations in (P1):
\begin{align}
\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1}
&=\frac{q_2(1-x_0)}{q_1(1-x_0^{-1})} &&\text{by (P1) and (P3)}\\
&=s\frac{1-x_0}{(x_0-1)/x_0} &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=-sx_0. &&\text{simplify}
\end{align}
Hence
\begin{align}
x_0&=-s\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1}. \label{eq:signed-x0}
\end{align}
Substitute \eqref{eq:signed-x0} into the cubic in (P4). A direct expansion and collection gives
\begin{align}
P\!\left(-s\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1}\right)
&=\frac{\psi_2^2}{\psi_1^2}
(\psi_1+s\psi_2)^2
(2\psi_1-s\psi_2-1)(2\psi_1-s\psi_2+1). \label{eq:signed-factor}
\end{align}
Because \(P(x_0)=0\), \(\psi_1\psi_2\neq0\), and \(x_0\neq1\), the factors
\[
\frac{\psi_2^2}{\psi_1^2}\neq0,
\qquad
\psi_1+s\psi_2\neq0
\]
are nonzero; the second nonzero statement follows from
\(x_0=-s\psi_2/\psi_1\neq1\). Therefore \eqref{eq:signed-factor} implies
\begin{align}
(2\psi_1-s\psi_2-1)(2\psi_1-s\psi_2+1)&=0,\\
2\psi_1-s\psi_2&=\pm1. \label{eq:signed-line}
\end{align}
Finally, \eqref{eq:signed-x0} gives
\begin{align}
\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2
&=\psi_1^2\left(-s\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1}\right)^2-\psi_2^2\\
&=(s^2-1)\psi_2^2\\
&=0,
\end{align}
so the first numerator factor in (P5) vanishes. Since \(x_0(x_0-1)^2\neq0\),
\begin{align}
F_\Phi&=0.
\end{align}
Taking \(s=-1\) gives the five-dimensional branch \(q_2=-q_1\), while taking \(s=+1\) gives the additional ten-dimensional sign allowed by \(|q_1|=|q_2|\) in (P6).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{x_0=-s\frac{\psi_2}{\psi_1},\qquad 2\psi_1-s\psi_2=\pm1,
\qquad F_\Phi=0.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_2:
\textbf{Claim.}
For a non-degenerate regular source root,
\[
x_0>0,
\qquad x_0\neq1,
\qquad \psi_1\neq0,
\qquad P(x_0)=0,
\]
the second formal zero of the energy numerator,
\[
\psi_1^2x_0=\psi_2^2,
\]
collapses to a forbidden or degenerate case. Consequently every non-degenerate regular zero-energy branch must satisfy
\[
\psi_2^2=\psi_1^2x_0^2,
\]
and, after imposing the source cubic, also satisfies
\[
\psi_1=\pm\frac{1}{x_0+2}.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &P(x_0)=0,\text{ where}\\
&P(x):=\psi_1^2x^3+
\bigl(\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2\bigr)x^2\\
&\hspace{36mm}-\psi_2^2\bigl(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1\bigr)x+
\psi_2^4.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &F_\Phi=-16\frac{(\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2)(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2)}{x_0(x_0-1)^2}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &x_0>0,
\qquad x_0\neq1,
\qquad \psi_1\neq0.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{The branch is non-degenerate, so }F_\Phi=0\text{ is interpreted with }P(x_0)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
The energy formula gives
\begin{align}
F_\Phi=0
&\Longleftrightarrow
(\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2)(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2)=0 &&\text{by (P2) and (P3)}.
\end{align}
First test the second factor. If
\(\psi_2^2=\psi_1^2x_0\), then substituting this relation into the source polynomial gives
\begin{align}
P(x_0)
&=\psi_1^4x_0^2(x_0-1)^2. \label{eq:second-factor-collapse}
\end{align}
By (P1), (P3), and \eqref{eq:second-factor-collapse}, this is impossible unless
\(\psi_1=0\) or \(x_0=1\). Both are excluded by the non-degenerate assumptions. Thus the second energy factor cannot generate a non-degenerate regular zero-energy branch.
Therefore a non-degenerate regular zero-energy branch must satisfy
\begin{align}
\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2&=0,\\
\psi_2^2&=\psi_1^2x_0^2. \label{eq:first-factor}
\end{align}
Now impose the cubic under \eqref{eq:first-factor}. Substitution gives
\begin{align}
P(x_0)
&=\psi_1^2x_0^2(x_0-1)^2
\bigl(\psi_1(x_0+2)-1\bigr)
\bigl(\psi_1(x_0+2)+1\bigr). \label{eq:first-factor-cubic}
\end{align}
Using \(P(x_0)=0\), \(\psi_1\neq0\), \(x_0>0\), and \(x_0\neq1\), equation \eqref{eq:first-factor-cubic} reduces to
\begin{align}
\psi_1(x_0+2)&=\pm1,\\
\psi_1&=\pm\frac{1}{x_0+2}.
\end{align}
Together with \(\psi_2^2=\psi_1^2x_0^2\), this is equivalently
\[
\psi_2=\pm\psi_1x_0,
\qquad
\psi_1=\pm\frac{1}{x_0+2},
\]
with independent sign choices subject to the chosen physical branch.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
\begin{gathered}
P(x_0)=0,\quad x_0>0,\quad x_0\neq1,\quad \psi_1\neq0,\quad F_\Phi=0\\
\Longrightarrow
\psi_2^2=\psi_1^2x_0^2
\text{ and }
\psi_1=\pm\frac{1}{x_0+2}.
\end{gathered}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.}
The formal root \(x_0=1\) occurs exactly on the source transition lines
\[
\psi_1=\psi_2
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\psi_1=-\psi_2.
\]
On those lines the positive source root degenerates to a double root at \(x_0=1\), the reconstructed parameter \(\eta\) tends to zero, and therefore the scalar one-point function tends to zero:
\[
\langle O\rangle\to0.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &P(x):=\psi_1^2x^3+
\bigl(\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2\bigr)x^2\\
&\hspace{36mm}-\psi_2^2\bigl(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1\bigr)x+
\psi_2^4.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &P(x_0)=0\text{ is the source-only regularity constraint.}\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\eta x_0^2=(x_0-1)^2(q_1^2-q_2^2x_0).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\langle O\rangle=\frac{2\sqrt{2}L^2}{\sqrt{3}}\eta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &L>0,
\qquad \text{the transition is approached with finite }q_1^2-q_2^2x_0.
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Evaluate the source polynomial at \(x=1\):
\begin{align}
P(1)
&=\psi_1^2+
\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2
-\psi_2^2(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1)+\psi_2^4\\
&=4\psi_1^4-8\psi_1^2\psi_2^2+4\psi_2^4\\
&=4(\psi_1^2-\psi_2^2)^2\\
&=4(\psi_1-\psi_2)^2(\psi_1+\psi_2)^2. \label{eq:p-one}
\end{align}
Thus \(x_0=1\) can satisfy the cubic only if
\begin{align}
\psi_1^2-\psi_2^2&=0,\\
\psi_1&=\psi_2\quad\text{or}\quad \psi_1=-\psi_2. \label{eq:transition-lines}
\end{align}
Conversely, impose either transition line, so \(\psi_2^2=\psi_1^2\). Then
\begin{align}
P(x)
&=\psi_1^2(x-1)^2(x+\psi_1^2). \label{eq:double-root}
\end{align}
For \(\psi_1\neq0\), the root \(x=1\) is double, while the remaining root \(x=-\psi_1^2\) is negative and hence is not an admissible positive centre.
Finally, from (P3), along a finite transition limit with \(x_0\to1\),
\begin{align}
\eta
&=\frac{(x_0-1)^2(q_1^2-q_2^2x_0)}{x_0^2}\\
&\longrightarrow0. \label{eq:eta-zero}
\end{align}
Using (P4),
\begin{align}
\langle O\rangle
&=\frac{2\sqrt{2}L^2}{\sqrt{3}}\eta\\
&\longrightarrow0.
\end{align}
Thus the algebraic condition \(x_0=1\) is not an ordinary capped soliton centre; it is the no-centre, no-scalar-VEV transition locus.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{x_0=1\Longleftrightarrow \psi_1=\pm\psi_2,
\qquad
P(x)=\psi_1^2(x-1)^2(x+\psi_1^2)\text{ on this locus},
\qquad
\eta\to0,
\qquad
\langle O\rangle\to0.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_4:
\textbf{Claim.}
At fixed boundary sources \((\delta,\psi_1,\psi_2)\), the canonical energy ordering of admissible positive roots is completely determined by the dimensionless function
\[
F_\Phi(x_0)=-16\frac{(\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2)(\psi_1^2x_0-\psi_2^2)}{x_0(x_0-1)^2}.
\]
In particular, for two admissible roots \(x_a\) and \(x_b\) with the same \((\delta,\psi_1,\psi_2)\),
\[
E_\Phi(x_a)<E_\Phi(x_b)
\Longleftrightarrow
F_\Phi(x_a)<F_\Phi(x_b).
\]
The comparison is independent of \(L\), \(\kappa\), and \(V_2\), and its only \(\delta\)-dependence is the common positive scale \(|E_0|\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &F_\Phi:=\frac{E_\Phi}{|E_0|}.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &E_0=-\frac{L^3\pi^4}{2\kappa\delta^3}V_2.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &L>0,
\qquad \kappa>0,
\qquad \delta>0,
\qquad V_2>0.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &F_\Phi(x)=-16\frac{(\psi_1^2x^2-\psi_2^2)(\psi_1^2x-\psi_2^2)}{x(x-1)^2}.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &x_a\text{ and }x_b\text{ are admissible positive roots of the same source cubic at fixed }(\delta,\psi_1,\psi_2).
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
By (P2) and (P3),
\begin{align}
|E_0|
&=\frac{L^3\pi^4}{2\kappa\delta^3}V_2>0. \label{eq:e0-positive}
\end{align}
Therefore (P1) gives, for any admissible root \(x\),
\begin{align}
E_\Phi(x)&=|E_0|F_\Phi(x). \label{eq:energy-scale}
\end{align}
For two admissible roots at the same boundary sources,
\begin{align}
E_\Phi(x_a)-E_\Phi(x_b)
&=|E_0|\bigl(F_\Phi(x_a)-F_\Phi(x_b)\bigr) &&\text{by \eqref{eq:energy-scale}}.
\end{align}
Since \(|E_0|>0\), multiplication by \(|E_0|\) preserves strict, weak, and equality orderings. Hence
\begin{align}
E_\Phi(x_a)<E_\Phi(x_b)
&\Longleftrightarrow
F_\Phi(x_a)<F_\Phi(x_b),\\
E_\Phi(x_a)=E_\Phi(x_b)
&\Longleftrightarrow
F_\Phi(x_a)=F_\Phi(x_b),\\
E_\Phi(x_a)>E_\Phi(x_b)
&\Longleftrightarrow
F_\Phi(x_a)>F_\Phi(x_b).
\end{align}
The expression in (P4) contains only \(x\), \(\psi_1\), and \(\psi_2\). Thus the branch ordering at fixed sources is dimensionless; \(L\), \(\kappa\), \(V_2\), and \(\delta\) set only the common positive energy scale \(|E_0|\), not the preferred root.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x_0\in\mathcal{R}(\psi_1,\psi_2)}E_\Phi(x_0)
=
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x_0\in\mathcal{R}(\psi_1,\psi_2)}F_\Phi(x_0),}
\]
where \(\mathcal{R}(\psi_1,\psi_2)\) is the set of admissible positive source-cubic roots.
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_5:
\textbf{Claim.}
The weak-coupling vacuum-energy comparison separates two boundary-theory reference vacua:
\[
\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}}\rangle=0
\]
for common anti-periodicity of scalars, vectors, and fermions, while
\[
\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}*}\rangle=-\frac{\pi^2V_2}{6\delta^3}(N^2-1)
\]
for periodic bosons and anti-periodic fermions. In the large-\(N\) replacement \(N^2-1\mapsto N^2\), the gravitational AdS-soliton reference energy is
\[
E_0=\frac34\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}*}\rangle.
\]
Consequently, any branch with \(F_\Phi=0\) has \(E_\Phi=0\) and is energy-aligned with the zero weak-coupling vacuum rather than with the negative AdS-soliton reference.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}}\rangle=0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}*}\rangle=-\frac{\pi^2V_2}{6\delta^3}(N^2-1).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &E_0=-\frac{L^3\pi^4}{2\kappa\delta^3}V_2,
\qquad \frac{L^3}{\kappa}=\frac{N^2}{4\pi^2}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &F_\Phi=\frac{E_\Phi}{|E_0|}.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &V_2>0,
\qquad \delta>0,
\qquad N\to\infty.
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First express the gravitational reference energy in field-theory variables:
\begin{align}
E_0
&=-\frac{L^3\pi^4}{2\kappa\delta^3}V_2 &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=-\frac{\pi^4V_2}{2\delta^3}\frac{N^2}{4\pi^2} &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=-\frac{\pi^2V_2N^2}{8\delta^3}. \label{eq:e0-n}
\end{align}
Under the large-\(N\) replacement \(N^2-1\mapsto N^2\), (P2) becomes
\begin{align}
\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}*}\rangle
&=-\frac{\pi^2V_2N^2}{6\delta^3}. \label{eq:estar-n}
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
\frac34\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}*}\rangle
&=\frac34\left(-\frac{\pi^2V_2N^2}{6\delta^3}\right)\\
&=-\frac{\pi^2V_2N^2}{8\delta^3}\\
&=E_0 &&\text{by \eqref{eq:e0-n}}. \label{eq:three-quarters}
\end{align}
Because \(V_2>0\), \(\delta>0\), and \(N^2>0\), equations \eqref{eq:e0-n} and \eqref{eq:estar-n} are strictly negative, while (P1) is zero.
If a branch has \(F_\Phi=0\), then (P4) gives
\begin{align}
E_\Phi&=|E_0|F_\Phi=0.
\end{align}
Thus the zero-energy holographic branch matches the energy value of the common anti-periodic weak-coupling vacuum, whereas the AdS-soliton reference matches the periodic-boson weak-coupling vacuum only up to the strong-coupling factor \(3/4\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}}\rangle=0,
\qquad
E_\Phi=0\text{ when }F_\Phi=0,
\qquad
E_0=\frac34\langle E_{\mathrm{SYM}*}\rangle<0.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_7:
\textbf{Claim.}
The ten-dimensional uplift contains a rigid scalar-sector simplification that is not visible from the five-dimensional energy formula alone.  For the soliton scalar profile
\[
\Phi_1=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\ln x,
\qquad
\Phi_2=0,
\]
one has
\[
X_1=X_2=x^{-1/3},
\qquad
X_3=x^{2/3},
\qquad
\widetilde\Delta=x^{-1/3}\bigl(1+(x-1)\mu_3^2\bigr).
\]
Consequently, on the zero-gauge-field slice \(q_1=q_2=0\), the ten-dimensional metric separates the \((\mu_1,\varphi_1,\mu_2,\varphi_2)\) directions from the \((\mu_3,
\varphi_3)\) directions with equal coefficients inside the first four-plane.  This is precisely the algebraic reason that the slice is assigned the
\(SO(4)\times SO(2)\) D3-brane-distribution class.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &X_1=\exp\!\left[-\frac12\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1+\sqrt2\Phi_2\right)\right],\\
&X_2=\exp\!\left[-\frac12\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1-\sqrt2\Phi_2\right)\right],\\
&X_3=\exp\!\left[-\frac12\left(-\frac{4}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1\right)\right].\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\Phi_1=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\ln x,
\qquad \Phi_2=0,
\qquad x>0.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2+\mu_3^2=1,
\qquad
\widetilde\Delta=X_1\mu_1^2+X_2\mu_2^2+X_3\mu_3^2.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &ds_{10}^2=\widetilde\Delta^{1/2}ds_5^2
+L^2\widetilde\Delta^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^3X_i^{-1}
\left(d\mu_i^2+\mu_i^2\left(d\varphi_i+\frac{A_i}{L}\right)^2\right).\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &A_1=A_2=0,
\qquad A_3=0
\quad\text{when }q_1=q_2=0.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{Equal coefficients for two orthogonal two-planes combine to an }SO(4)
\text{ symmetry,}\nonumber\\
&\text{while a single remaining angular two-plane carries an }SO(2)\text{ symmetry.}
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First compute the scalar exponents.  From (P2),
\begin{align}
\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1
&=\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\ln x\\
&=\frac{2}{3}\ln x. \label{eq:first-exponent}
\end{align}
Since \(\Phi_2=0\), equations (P1) and \eqref{eq:first-exponent} give
\begin{align}
X_1
&=\exp\!\left(-\frac13\ln x\right)=x^{-1/3},\\
X_2
&=\exp\!\left(-\frac13\ln x\right)=x^{-1/3}. \label{eq:xone-xtwo}
\end{align}
Similarly,
\begin{align}
X_3
&=\exp\!\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1\right)\\
&=\exp\!\left(\frac23\ln x\right)=x^{2/3}. \label{eq:xthree}
\end{align}
Substituting \eqref{eq:xone-xtwo}--\eqref{eq:xthree} into (P3),
\begin{align}
\widetilde\Delta
&=x^{-1/3}\mu_1^2+x^{-1/3}\mu_2^2+x^{2/3}\mu_3^2\\
&=x^{-1/3}(\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2)+x^{2/3}\mu_3^2\\
&=x^{-1/3}(1-\mu_3^2)+x^{2/3}\mu_3^2 &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=x^{-1/3}\bigl(1+(x-1)\mu_3^2\bigr). \label{eq:delta-tilde-reduced}
\end{align}
On the slice \(q_1=q_2=0\), (P5) reduces the internal part of (P4) to
\begin{align}
L^2\widetilde\Delta^{-1/2}
\Bigl[&x^{1/3}\bigl(d\mu_1^2+\mu_1^2d\varphi_1^2+d\mu_2^2+\mu_2^2d\varphi_2^2\bigr)\\
&\qquad +x^{-2/3}\bigl(d\mu_3^2+\mu_3^2d\varphi_3^2\bigr)\Bigr], \label{eq:internal-split}
\end{align}
where the equality \(X_1^{-1}=X_2^{-1}=x^{1/3}\) gives a common coefficient for the first two polar planes and \(X_3^{-1}=x^{-2/3}\) gives the separate coefficient for the third plane.
By (P6), \eqref{eq:internal-split} has the announced
\(SO(4)\times SO(2)\) algebraic structure.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
X_1=X_2=x^{-1/3},\qquad
X_3=x^{2/3},\qquad
\widetilde\Delta=x^{-1/3}\bigl(1+(x-1)\mu_3^2\bigr),
\qquad
q_1=q_2=0\Longrightarrow SO(4)\times SO(2)
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_8:
\textbf{Claim.}
The source-space cubic is not merely an auxiliary equation: together with an admissible positive root it provides the reconstruction map from boundary data to bulk parameters.  For
\[
\delta>0,
\qquad x_0>0,
\qquad x_0\neq1,
\qquad P(x_0)=0,
\]
define
\[
q_1=\frac{2\pi\psi_1x_0}{\delta(x_0-1)},
\qquad
q_2=-\frac{2\pi\psi_2}{\delta(x_0-1)}.
\]
Then the Wilson-line source equations are satisfied exactly:
\[
q_1(1-x_0^{-1})\delta=2\pi\psi_1,
\qquad
q_2(1-x_0)\delta=2\pi\psi_2.
\]
Moreover the period scale acts only as an overall reconstruction scale,
\[
q_1,q_2=O(\delta^{-1}),
\qquad
q_1^2-q_2^2x_0=O(\delta^{-2}),
\]
whereas the source-root selection and the dimensionless energy \(F_\Phi(x_0)\) are independent of \(\delta\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &P(x):=\psi_1^2x^3+
\bigl(\psi_2^4+4\psi_1^4-4\psi_1^2\psi_2^2-
\psi_2^2-\psi_1^2\bigr)x^2\\
&\hspace{36mm}-\psi_2^2\bigl(4\psi_1^2-2\psi_2^2-1\bigr)x+
\psi_2^4.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &P(x_0)=0,
\qquad x_0>0,
\qquad x_0\neq1,
\qquad \delta>0.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &q_1=\frac{2\pi\psi_1x_0}{\delta(x_0-1)},
\qquad
q_2=-\frac{2\pi\psi_2}{\delta(x_0-1)}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &F_\Phi(x)=-16\frac{(\psi_1^2x^2-\psi_2^2)(\psi_1^2x-\psi_2^2)}{x(x-1)^2}.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{The cubic }P(x_0)=0\text{ is the source-only regularity condition obtained after}\nonumber\\
&\text{eliminating }q_1,q_2\text{ and the period from the regular soliton equations.}
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
The first Wilson-line equation follows directly from (P3):
\begin{align}
q_1(1-x_0^{-1})\delta
&=\frac{2\pi\psi_1x_0}{\delta(x_0-1)}\left(1-\frac1{x_0}\right)\delta\\
&=\frac{2\pi\psi_1x_0}{\delta(x_0-1)}\frac{x_0-1}{x_0}\delta\\
&=2\pi\psi_1. \label{eq:source-one-recovered}
\end{align}
The second Wilson-line equation is recovered similarly:
\begin{align}
q_2(1-x_0)\delta
&=-\frac{2\pi\psi_2}{\delta(x_0-1)}(1-x_0)\delta\\
&=2\pi\psi_2. \label{eq:source-two-recovered}
\end{align}
Thus the reconstruction map preserves the prescribed boundary sources exactly.
Next, since \(x_0\), \(\psi_1\), and \(\psi_2\) are fixed when a source root is chosen, equations (P3) imply
\begin{align}
q_1&=\delta^{-1}\frac{2\pi\psi_1x_0}{x_0-1},\\
q_2&=\delta^{-1}\left(-\frac{2\pi\psi_2}{x_0-1}\right),\\
q_1^2-q_2^2x_0
&=\delta^{-2}\frac{4\pi^2}{(x_0-1)^2}
\bigl(\psi_1^2x_0^2-\psi_2^2x_0\bigr). \label{eq:delta-scaling}
\end{align}
Therefore changing \(\delta\) at fixed \((\psi_1,\psi_2,x_0)\) rescales the reconstructed charges but does not change the root equation (P1)--(P2).
Finally, (P4) contains only \(x\), \(\psi_1\), and \(\psi_2\).  Hence once the admissible positive roots of \(P\) are known, the dimensionless branch energy is determined before choosing the overall period scale.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
q_1=\frac{2\pi\psi_1x_0}{\delta(x_0-1)},
\quad
q_2=-\frac{2\pi\psi_2}{\delta(x_0-1)}
\Longrightarrow
\begin{cases}
q_1(1-x_0^{-1})\delta=2\pi\psi_1,\\
q_2(1-x_0)\delta=2\pi\psi_2,
\end{cases}
\quad
F_\Phi=F_\Phi(x_0;\psi_1,\psi_2)
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_9:
\textbf{Claim.}
The uplift ansatz has a zero-gauge-field reduction that directly realizes the D3-brane-distribution target rather than merely appending a ten-dimensional metric.  For
\[
\Phi_1=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\ln x,
\qquad
\Phi_2=0,
\qquad
\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2+\mu_3^2=1,
\]
the scalar functions obey
\[
X_1=X_2=x^{-1/3},
\qquad
X_3=x^{2/3},
\qquad
\widetilde\Delta=x^{-1/3}\bigl(1+(x-1)\mu_3^2\bigr).
\]
On the slice \(q_1=q_2=0\), the gauge-field part of \(G_5\) vanishes and the scalar-gradient part collapses to a single \(\mu_3\)-direction:
\[
G_{5,\mathrm{gauge}}=0,
\qquad
G_{5,\mathrm{scalar}}=-L^2\star_5(x^{-1}dx)\wedge d\mu_3^2.
\]
Thus the ten-dimensional data depend on the internal sphere through \(\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2\) and \(\mu_3^2\), giving the advertised \(SO(4)\times SO(2)\) scalar-deformed uplift structure.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &X_1=\exp\!\left[-\frac12\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1+\sqrt2\Phi_2\right)\right],\\
&X_2=\exp\!\left[-\frac12\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1-\sqrt2\Phi_2\right)\right],\\
&X_3=\exp\!\left[-\frac12\left(-\frac{4}{\sqrt6}\Phi_1\right)\right].\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\Phi_1=\sqrt{\frac23}\ln x,
\qquad \Phi_2=0,
\qquad \mu_1^2+\mu_2^2+\mu_3^2=1.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\widetilde\Delta=X_1\mu_1^2+X_2\mu_2^2+X_3\mu_3^2.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &G_{5,\mathrm{gauge}}=L^2\sum_{i=1}^3X_i^{-2}\mu_i d\mu_i\wedge\left(d\varphi_i+\frac{A_i}{L}\right)\wedge\star_5 F_i.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &G_{5,\mathrm{scalar}}=-L^2\sum_{i=1}^3X_i^{-1}\star_5 dX_i\wedge d\mu_i^2.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &q_1=q_2=0\Longrightarrow A_1=A_2=A_3=0\text{ and }F_1=F_2=F_3=0.
\end{aligned}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
Using (P1)--(P2),
\begin{align}
X_1
&=\exp\!\left[-\frac12\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\sqrt{\frac23}\ln x\right]
=\exp\!\left[-\frac13\ln x\right]
=x^{-1/3},\\
X_2
&=X_1=x^{-1/3},\\
X_3
&=\exp\!\left[\frac{2}{\sqrt6}\sqrt{\frac23}\ln x\right]
=\exp\!\left[\frac23\ln x\right]
=x^{2/3}.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
\widetilde\Delta
&=x^{-1/3}(\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2)+x^{2/3}\mu_3^2 &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=x^{-1/3}(1-\mu_3^2)+x^{2/3}\mu_3^2 &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=x^{-1/3}\bigl(1+(x-1)\mu_3^2\bigr). \label{eq:Delta-reduced}
\end{align}
On \(q_1=q_2=0\), every \(F_i\) vanishes, hence
\begin{align}
G_{5,\mathrm{gauge}}&=0 &&\text{by (P4) and (P6)}.
\end{align}
For the scalar-gradient part, first combine the equal \(X_1\) and \(X_2\) terms:
\begin{align}
G_{5,\mathrm{scalar}}
&=-L^2\left[X_1^{-1}\star_5dX_1\wedge d(\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2)+X_3^{-1}\star_5dX_3\wedge d\mu_3^2\right] &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=-L^2\left[-X_1^{-1}\star_5dX_1+X_3^{-1}\star_5dX_3\right]\wedge d\mu_3^2 &&\text{since }d(\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2)=-d\mu_3^2. \label{eq:Gscalar-combine}
\end{align}
The logarithmic derivatives are
\begin{align}
X_1^{-1}dX_1&=-\frac13x^{-1}dx,\\
X_3^{-1}dX_3&=\frac23x^{-1}dx.
\end{align}
Substituting these into \eqref{eq:Gscalar-combine},
\begin{align}
G_{5,\mathrm{scalar}}
&=-L^2\left[\frac13\star_5(x^{-1}dx)+\frac23\star_5(x^{-1}dx)\right]\wedge d\mu_3^2\\
&=-L^2\star_5(x^{-1}dx)\wedge d\mu_3^2. \label{eq:Gscalar-final}
\end{align}
Equations \eqref{eq:Delta-reduced} and \eqref{eq:Gscalar-final} involve \(\mu_1,\mu_2\) only through \(\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2\), while the remaining distinguished direction is \(\mu_3^2\).  This is precisely the internal splitting associated with \(SO(4)\times SO(2)\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
\widetilde\Delta=x^{-1/3}\bigl(1+(x-1)\mu_3^2\bigr),
\qquad
G_{5,\mathrm{gauge}}=0,
\qquad
G_{5,\mathrm{scalar}}=-L^2\star_5(x^{-1}dx)\wedge d\mu_3^2
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
